title: Turkish Delight
subtitle: Rosewater and lemon jellied confectionery
excerpt: The Ottoman confection: cornflour-thickened sugar syrup flavoured with rosewater and lemon, set to a tender, bouncy jelly, then cut into cubes and rolled in icing sugar and cornflour. Scented, delicate, and nothing like the commercial version.

recipe.sourceNotes: Turkish delight (lokum in Turkish) has been produced in Turkey since at least the eighteenth century; the confectioner Hacı Bekir is credited with perfecting the modern cornflour-based version in Istanbul in the 1770s. It became known in the West after British travellers brought it home in the nineteenth century. The defining quality of real lokum is its texture: a tender jelly that gives slightly under pressure before yielding cleanly, with none of the rubbery toughness of commercial versions. This comes from the precise cooking of the cornflour and sugar mixture to the right stage, which takes patience and a thermometer. Rosewater and lemon are the traditional flavouring; other common flavourings include pomegranate juice, mastic, and mint.

recipeTools.notes: The syrup must reach exactly 115°C for the correct texture. Under-cooked and the delight will not set; over-cooked and it will be too firm.

content.text: Cornflour lokum requires patience: the cornflour paste must be cooked slowly into the sugar syrup and stirred almost continuously for 45 minutes until it pulls away from the sides of the pan. Use a heavy pan to avoid scorching and a wooden spoon. The mixture will splutter as it thickens; take care.

items.preparation: plus extra mixed with icing sugar for dusting

content.text: Dissolve 125 g cornflour in 200 ml cold water. In a separate pan, dissolve the caster sugar in 400 ml water with the lemon juice over low heat. Bring to the boil and cook to 115°C.

Slowly pour the hot syrup into the cornflour paste in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Return to the heat over medium-low and cook, stirring, for 40 to 45 minutes until the mixture is thick, translucent, and pulls away from the sides of the pan. Stir in the rosewater or vanilla.

Pour into a lightly oiled 20 cm square tin lined with baking paper. Smooth the surface. Leave to set at room temperature for at least 4 hours or overnight. Turn out onto a board dusted with icing sugar and cornflour mixed 50:50. Cut into 3 cm squares with an oiled knife. Roll each piece in the dusting mixture and store in an airtight container at room temperature.
